featured_reviews.name: dhawal gala
featured_reviews.review_text:
Stepping into Bayroute in Cuffe Parade is less like walking into a restaurant and more like embarking on an enchanting journey across the Mediterranean and Middle East. From the moment you cross the threshold, the attention to detail in the ambience, the authentic depth of the cuisine, and the seamless service work in perfect harmony to deliver an unforgettable fine-dining experience.

The Ambience: An Arabian Night's Dream
The ambience at Bayroute is truly its soul, beautifully capturing the old-world charm and opulence of the Levant. The decor is a magnificent blend of Moroccan, Turkish, and Arabian influences. Warm, rich lighting spills over intricately patterned floor tiles and tastefully adorned walls, which feature beautiful Turkish art. The seating is plush and comfortable, with Moroccan printed sofas that invite a leisurely, communal dining experience.

The entire space exudes a refined yet cozy atmosphere—perfect for a romantic evening, a sophisticated family dinner, or celebrating a special occasion. It’s an aesthetically curated masterpiece where every corner offers a visual delight, transporting you far away from the hustle of Mumbai.

The Food: An Authentic and Flavorful Expedition
The menu is an extensive map of culinary delights from countries like Egypt, Turkey, Lebanon, and Greece. It's a testament to authentic, well-researched cuisine, and every dish we tried was a revelation.The ingredients taste fresh, and the authentic spices are used with a delicate hand, ensuring the dishes are flavorful without being overwhelmingly heavy.

The Service: Courteous and Impeccable

A superb meal is only elevated by excellent service, and Bayroute truly shines here. The staff is exceptionally courteous, knowledgeable, and attentive. Our server was well-versed in the menu, offering insightful recommendations and patiently explaining the different regional nuances of the dishes. The pacing of the meal was perfect—neither rushed nor slow—allowing us to fully enjoy the experience. The attention to detail, from refreshing water glasses to clearing plates promptly, was seamless and professional.

Bayrute is more than just a restaurant; it’s a cultural experience. While it is on the higher end of the pricing scale, the unparalleled ambience, the authentic and delicious food, and the impeccable, friendly service make it absolutely worth the indulgence. It remains a must-visit destination for anyone looking to sample the finest Middle Eastern and Mediterranean cuisine in Mumbai in a truly magnificent setting.

featured_reviews.name: Monica
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re craving an authentic Middle Eastern experience in Mumbai, BAYROUTE is a place you simply can’t miss. We visited their Cuffe Parade outlet, and honestly, it felt like stepping straight into an Arabian dining room, warm, inviting, and rich in flavours.

Let’s start with their Classic Hummus, because that’s a non-negotiable order here. Creamy, smooth, and beautifully balanced, it’s topped with pine nuts, finished with labneh, and generously drizzled with good quality extra virgin olive oil. Simple, classic, and done perfectly, exactly how hummus should be.

For a refreshing sip, we tried their Reyhan, a soft beverage made with muddled orange and basil. Super refreshing, fragrant, and a great palate cleanser alongside the heavier dishes.

The Cheese Manakeesh was another standout. A soft Middle Eastern flatbread brushed with olive oil, loaded with lots of cheese. Comforting, indulgent, and perfect for sharing.

One of the highlights of the meal was the Dijaj Tria, a roasted trio of chicken kebabs featuring harissa spiced chicken, creamy shish taouk and Saffron Joojeh, served with garlic sauce, spicy schug and a punchy acili ezme dip. Every skewer brought something different to the table, and all of them were cooked beautifully.

Seafood lovers will enjoy the Butter Garlic Prawns, juicy, well-seasoned, and finished with rich garlic butter flavours without overpowering the prawns themselves.

We wrapped up with the Yemeni Mandi, which was aromatic, flavourful, and comforting, a wholesome dish that truly completes the Middle Eastern feast.

Overall, BAYROUTE delivers a genuine Arabian dining experience, from flavours to ambience. Perfect for anyone who enjoys Lebanese, Turkish, and Middle Eastern cuisine under one roof.

I Visited this place with one of my Friend. Its a roadside stall or outlet kind of. But the taste will not disappoint you in any way. Below is my brief description and as per my personal experience to what all i have tried there. (I tried almost everything Except Paneer and Mutton Seek)
Place is nearby World Trade Center.

A Chicken Tikka Roll is a popular Indian street food that features marinated and grilled chicken, typically in a blend of yogurt and spices. The cooked chicken is then rolled in a flatbread, often a paratha or roti, and garnished with onions, mint chutney, and sometimes lettuce. It combines the rich flavors of spiced chicken with the convenience of a handheld roll, making it a delicious and satisfying snack or meal. Its very tasty. I have tried Chicken Seek. In this they have Malai Seek as well.

Mutton kebabs are savory meat skewers made from marinated and seasoned mutton The mutton is typically minced or finely chopped and mixed with a blend of aromatic spices, herbs, and sometimes breadcrumbs. Common spices include cumin, coriander, ginger, and garlic. The mixture is then shaped into elongated cylinders or patties and grilled or roasted until cooked to perfection. Mutton kebabs are known for their robust flavor and tender texture, making them a popular and flavorful dish in many cuisines around the world. They have Mutton seek roll or if you prefer you can take it without Roti.

FYI: THEY DONT SERVE BEEF

Tandoori Mushrooms are a delectable vegetarian dish where mushrooms are marinated in a blend of yogurt and tandoori spices, which may include cumin, coriander, turmeric, and red chili powder. The marinated mushrooms are then threaded onto skewers and cooked in a tandoor, a traditional clay oven. The high heat of the tandoor imparts a smoky flavor and a slightly charred exterior to the mushrooms, while keeping them tender on the inside. Tandoori Mushrooms are often served with a side of mint chutney and make for a flavorful and aromatic appetizer or snack.

A Tandoori Paneer Roll is a popular Indian street food that features marinated and grilled paneer (Indian cottage cheese) rolled in a flatbread. The paneer is typically marinated in a mixture of yogurt and tandoori spices, including cumin, coriander, garam masala, and red chili powder. After marination, the paneer is skewered and grilled in a tandoor or oven.

Once the tandoori paneer is cooked, it's placed on a flatbread, often a paratha or roti, and rolled with accompaniments such as onions, bell peppers, mint chutney, and sometimes a squeeze of lime. The result is a flavorful and satisfying roll that combines the smokiness of tandoori-cooked paneer with the freshness of the accompanying ingredients. It's a popular choice for those looking for a delicious and vegetarian-friendly street food option.

For reference you can check the pictures i have uploaded and also one small video clip. This place is highly recommended for Meat and Chicken as well as Paneer Lovers.

featured_reviews.name: Poonam Tharar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Swati Snacks is truly one of the most iconic Gujarati restaurants in Bombay, and now rightfully loved across various other cities as well. It’s one of those rare places that becomes impossible to resist — whether you’re simply passing by the area or repeatedly finding yourself ordering from the same place despite endless newer options around.

The freshness in both the quality and quantity of the food is consistently outstanding. Their curd-based dishes are absolutely out of the world, and the juices, beverages, and seasonal specialties are always thoughtfully done and extremely appreciated. The service too remains top notch even during busy hours.
Parking a bit challenging however still can manage.

For visitors, it’s a must-visit Bombay institution. And for residents, it naturally becomes a regular affair. I love it.

featured_reviews.name: Priya Sridhar
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you want to try some unique gujarati food items then you surely need to visit swati snacks.

Everything we ordered was super yummy, freshly cooked and light on tummy(not oily at all unlike other gujarati restaurants).

We ordered following items:
1. Panki with chutney - panki was nicely cooked and soft. Chutney was tasty and not too spicy thankfully.
2. Kand tikki chaat (purple yam chaat) - Recommended to me by their staff. Very very unique chat, you will surely not get the same thing elsewhere.
3. Undhiyo and bajra rotla - Undhiyo was tasty and fresh, not oily at all. Bajra rotla was surprisingly soft. Served with few pieces of amba halad, raw haldi, and jaggery.
4. Bajra kichu - Unique form of kichu and very healthy too for winter.
5. Masala tea - served with sesame crackers. Tea was great too. By the way they also didn't charge me milk for the baby , which was sweet.

I wish I had more appetite to try more items. I will come back next time for sure

PS: They have a washroom too which was clean.
Waiting time is around 20 minutes which was manageable. Their service was quite quick by the way.

featured_reviews.name: Dr. Harshmeet kaur
featured_reviews.review_text: Swati Snacks is one of the most hygienic places for street-style food in Mumbai. Super quick service and consistently fresh flavors. featured_reviews.review_text: Still the gold standard for Thai food in Mumbai. The Tub Tim Grob (water chestnut dessert) was the perfect refreshing end to the meal. It’s expensive, but for the quality and the heritage, it’s worth every rupee.

featured_reviews.name: Buck Whas
featured_reviews.review_text: This is the most authentic Thai I’ve had in India. When I saw the menu and the dishes offered of which you don’t find in typical Thai restaurants I knew I had to check it out. The yum tua poo (wing bean salad) is a gem often overlooked but is amazing and if pescatarian do try it with prawn. I spoke with the head chef who has worked to maintain Thai flavors while respecting vegetarian majority. Nonetheless you request Thai style and she will turn it out authentic Thai style. I think this might be key if dining here and you have experience with Thai cuisine is that you need to specify that you wanted to be prepared a Thai style.

featured_reviews.name: Purvi Rathod
featured_reviews.review_text:
Everything from starters, mains and desserts was delicious. The team took extra care to make sure the food was non-spicy, as requested. Hard to pick one, but the desserts were delicious and very indulgent. It was my fist time tasting tub tim grob (water chestnuts in coconut milk with ice) and I loved it! We also ordered coconut pudding with sago and coconut ice cream and it was delicious too!

If you love thai food, I would highly recommend this place to you!

featured_reviews.name: Yogita N Goyal
featured_reviews.review_text: The food was authentic and very tasty. The bao Thai dish, similar to a dumpling, was soft and delicious. featured_reviews.review_text: After two weeks in India, we were ready for a little break from all of the wonderful Indian food we’ve had. All of our food was delicious - some of the tastiest Thai food I’ve had outside of Thailand. We shared the lotus and banana leaf salad, the red curry with shrimp, and the spicy basil rice. Everything was so delicious and satisfying. Our server was polite and attentive. The atmosphere is nice as well. Would love to return on our next trip to Mumbai!

featured_reviews.name: Sachi Gandhhi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Went to Thai pavilion for dinner recently and had a great experience! Loved the great service and delicious food.

They served pumpkin chips before the meal which were so light and crispy. I really enjoyed them.

For appetisers we had the pomelo salad which was my absolute favourite dish and I definitely recommend it. We also had the corn cakes which were good but could have had little more flavour. I ordered the Tom yum soup which was spicy and nice. We also got the lotus root chips which also tasted good with the house sauces that they provide.

For mains we had the pad Thai which I felt was a little bland and could have been more flavourful along with the water chestnut in a spicy sauce.

Although we liked some dishes more than others, they service was great and I will definitely be back for my favourites!

featured_reviews.name: Saquib Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Central Lunch Home, nestled in the vibrant neighborhood of Cuffe Parade, stands out for its delectable seafood offerings and authentic Mangalorean cuisine. One of their standout dishes is the Bombil Fry, a crispy delight that perfectly balances the delicate flavors of the fish with a tantalizing blend of spices. Each bite offers a satisfying crunch, making it an absolute must-try for seafood enthusiasts.

Another gem on their menu is the Mangalorean Style Chicken Sukkha, a rich and aromatic dish that bursts with flavors. The tender chicken pieces are marinated in a blend of traditional spices, cooked to perfection, and then simmered in a luscious coconut-based gravy. It's a dish that showcases the culinary prowess of Central Lunch Home's chefs and keeps patrons coming back for more.

For those looking for a hearty and fulfilling meal, the Egg Masala is a top choice. This dish features boiled eggs cooked in a flavorful masala gravy, infused with spices that pack a punch. It's a comforting dish that pairs well with rice or bread, making it a favorite among diners.

One of the most appealing aspects of Central Lunch Home is its affordability. Despite offering high-quality seafood and authentic dishes, the prices remain reasonable, making it accessible to a wide range of customers. Additionally, the portion sizes are generous, ensuring that diners leave fully satisfied.

However, it's worth noting that Central Lunch Home can get quite busy during peak hours, which might result in longer wait times. Nevertheless, the bustling atmosphere adds to the charm of the place, creating an authentic dining experience.

In summary, Central Lunch Home at Cuffe Parade is a haven for seafood lovers and aficionados of Mangalorean cuisine. With its affordable prices, generous portions, and high-quality food, it's no wonder why this restaurant is a favorite among locals and visitors alike. Whether you're craving Bombil Fry, Mangalorean Style Chicken Sukkha, or Egg Masala, Central Lunch Home delivers on taste, making every visit a memorable culinary adventure.

featured_reviews.name: Adil Syed
featured_reviews.review_text:
Location & Popularity
Bagdadi is located in a prime area of Colaba, making it easily accessible and always buzzing with people. The restaurant is extremely popular, especially during evening hours, which clearly reflects its strong reputation among food lovers.

Waiting Time
Due to the heavy rush during peak hours, particularly in the evenings, customers usually have to wait for their turn. While the wait can be a bit long, it also speaks volumes about how loved the food here is.

Food Quality
The food at Bagdadi is genuinely great. The flavors are rich, consistent, and worth coming back for. It’s one of those places where the taste truly lives up to the hype.

Ambience & Renovation (Personal Opinion)
In my personal opinion, the restaurant could really benefit from a renovation. The place feels a bit dated, and a refresh would greatly enhance the dining experience without taking away from its old-school charm.

Final Verdict
Bagdadi is a must-visit for its excellent food and prime Colaba location. Despite the waiting time and the need for renovation, the taste and authenticity make it well worth the experience—especially for those who don’t mind a little wait for good food.
